title: Recent Case Law Examples
lead: The 2025–2026 docket — ==rights, social justice, environmental governance==, and a fresh crop of ==Art 142, suo motu and judicial-review== questions. Use these as your current-affairs case bank.

head: Theme
Case
Key holding
rows: ==Menstrual health/dignity under Arts 21, 21A, 14==; directed infrastructure, education, gender-sensitised curricula. Separately (==Shailendra Mani Tripathi== PIL) declined to mandate uniform ==paid menstrual leave== fearing hiring bias — referred design to MWCD.
==First actual application of Common Cause (2018)==; ==CANH/PEG-tube feeding is ‘medical treatment’== that can be withdrawn under the ==best-interest test== when it only prolongs dying.
[[In Re: Phalodi Accident]] (after [[Gyan Prakash v. UoI, 2025]])
==‘Right to safe passage on roads’ part of Art 21==; positive duty on NHAI/MoRTH to remove encroachments and blackspots. ==Suo motu after 34 deaths==; ==13 guidelines== issued.
Dignity includes ==freedom from stray dog/cattle attacks==; fencing of schools/hospitals, sterilisation-relocation, ==personal liability for defaulting officials==.

First recognised a ==constitutional right to rehabilitation== under Arts 21 & 23; a ==Victim Protection Plan==; rehabilitation ==cannot be forced==; distinguished trafficking from voluntary adult sex work.
Walking on safe, demarcated footpaths is a ==fundamental right under Art 19(1)(d)== with an Art 21 dimension, ==taking priority over vehicular movement==.
[[In Re: Illegal Sand Mining in National Chambal Sanctuary]]
Suo motu on mining destroying ==Gharial habitat==; ==stayed denotification of 732 hectares==; GPS/CCTV monitoring; officials potentially ==vicariously liable==.
Suo motu on a chapter referencing judicial corruption/backlog — ==blanket ban==, seizure and digital takedown, show-cause notices; textbook later withdrawn.
Struck down ==s.60(4), Code on Social Security 2020== (3-month child age cap) under Arts 14 & 21 — ==12 weeks' leave irrespective of the child's age==; Centre urged to legislate ==paternity leave==.
[[In Re: Definition of Aravalli Hills and Ranges]]
Accepted a ==100m height + 500m buffer== definition and an MPSM; after protests ==stayed its own order== and constituted a fresh ==High-Powered Expert Committee== — interim mining freeze continues.

CSR inherently includes ==Corporate Environmental Responsibility== — a ==constitutional obligation under Art 51A(g)== and s.166(2) Companies Act, not voluntary charity; banned solar >2MW and overhead lines in GIB habitat.
Reaffirmed [[Selvi (2010)]] — ==forced narco tests violate Arts 20(3) & 21==; voluntary tests need ==magistrate-recorded consent== and have ==no standalone evidentiary value==.

Originally struck down the 2017 Notification/2021 OM permitting ==retrospective ECs== as unconstitutional; on review a ==2:1 bench recalled== the ruling — criticised in dissent as ==retrogression from the precautionary principle==.

sections.title: Judicial Review, Activism, Suo Motu & Art 142

head: Theme
Case
Key holding
rows: Refused a blanket stay (==presumption of constitutionality==) but ==partially stayed specific provisions== — a ==calibrated, restrained model== of reviewing a full statute.
Suo motu after 34 deaths; invoked ==Art 142 for nationwide interim directions== — reviving debate on the scope of ‘complete justice’.
A 5-judge bench used Art 142 to lay down ==mandatory, judicially-created seniority (roster) rules== for the Higher Judicial Service — ==filling an administrative vacuum==.
[[In Re: Directions in the Matter of Demolition of Structures]]

==Punitive demolitions ‘wholly unconstitutional’== — due process, separation of powers, right to shelter (Arts 19 & 21); ==pan-India guidelines== (show-cause, 15 days, videography); ==₹10 lakh compensation== ordered in March 2025 — ==continuing mandamus in action==.

==Upheld the Special Intensive Revision== as within ==Art 324 / s.21(3) RPA==, but had used interim directions (Aadhaar/ration card as ID, online claims for excluded voters) to soften it — ==deference plus rights-protective tailoring==.
Suo motu with ==no petitioner== → ban, seizure, contempt threat — debated as the judiciary acting as ==both protector and prosecutor of its own reputation==.
The SC ==reviewed and recalled its own May 2025 judgment== — a rare self-reversal, raising questions of ==judicial consistency== (strong dissent by Bhuyan, J.).
A ==multi-stage suo motu proceeding== with escalating directions — classic continuing supervision over municipal failure.
[[In Re: Illegal Sand Mining in National Chambal Sanctuary]]
==Art 142 invoked== for detailed, evolving directions to three states and central agencies.
